top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice clock is a clean, general mechanism (choose the wavelength where trapping light shifts both clock levels equally) that was independently reproduced at the 1e-18 level in several laboratories. Attribution to Katori (concept, first demonstration) and Ye (decisive accuracy and many-body regime) fits the three-person limit, and the proposed citation credits invention and realisation without ranking the two. Residual concerns, namely priority among Lemonde, Ludlow and other groups, the pending redefinition of the second, and prospective fundamental-physics searches, do not outweigh a mature, verified achievement, so an award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; only an institutional Gothenburg link to Johansson and Olsson, and no collaboration with Katori or Ye
